text: {"final": {"findings": [{"id": "R1", "statement": "register_household(record: dict) -> Household in registry/register.py loads all households, sets record['id'] via record.setdefault('id', next_household_id(households)) and record['registered'] via today().isoformat(), builds Household.from_dict(record), then validates: unknown region raises ValueError, no members raises ValueError, duplicate id raises ValueError(f\"household {household.id} is already registered\"). It appends and calls save_households(households) only after all checks pass, so raising before that point saves nothing. There is currently NO check that a caller-supplied household ID is well-formed.", "file": "registry/register.py"}, {"id": "R2", "statement": "core/ids.py defines is_valid_household_id(household_id: str) -> bool (line 31). Per search results, line 34 shows it uses a regex match m and returns bool(m) and household_check_digit(m.group(1)) == int(m.group(2)) — i.e. it validates the HH-NNNNC format AND the check digit. This existing function can be reused for the LIFE-142 validation.", "file": "core/ids.py"}, {"id": "R3", "statement": "Household ID format is HH-NNNNC: 'HH-' prefix, four digits, then one check digit (core/ids.py line 3 comment). household_check_digit(base: str) -> int | None (line 19) returns None for some bases (e.g. '1009' has no valid check digit), meaning not every 4-digit base yields a valid ID.", "file": "core/ids.py"}, {"id": "R4", "statement": "Test examples confirm behavior: make_household_id(1042) == 'HH-10421'; household_check_digit('1047') == 2; is_valid_household_id('HH-10421') and is_valid_household_id('HH-00019') are True; is_valid_household_id is False for 'HH-10471' (the mistyped ID from the ticket), 'HH-1042', 'HH-104211', 'HH-1042X', '10421', and ''. make_household_id(1009) raises ValueError because that base has no check digit.", "file": "tests/test_core.py"}, {"id": "R5", "statement": "next_household_id(households: list[Household] | None = None) -> str generates IDs automatically when 'id' is missing: number = max(int(h.id[3:7]) for h in households, default=999) + 1, skipping numbers whose household_check_digit(f\"{number:04d}\") is None, then returns make_household_id(number). Since it only produces valid IDs, any new validation must not reject auto-assigned IDs (or must run only when the caller supplied an 'id').", "file": "registry/register.py"}, {"id": "R6", "statement": "make_household_id(number: int) -> str (core/ids.py line 37) builds the ID from a number plus its check digit; per tests it raises ValueError if the base has no valid check digit (e.g. make_household_id(1009)).", "file": "core/ids.py"}, {"id": "R7", "statement": "Persistence: load_households(*, active_only: bool = False) reads store.read_json(REGISTRY)['households'] (REGISTRY = 'registry.json') into Household objects; save_households(households) writes them back via store.write_json. get_household(household_id) raises KeyError(f\"no household {household_id!r}\") if not found. Existing error style in register_household is plain ValueError with the offending value in the message (e.g. f\"unknown region {household.region!r}\"), matching the ticket's requirement to include the rejected ID.", "file": "registry/register.py"}]}}
